query: What visit reasons point to different departments?

per_column.name: presentation_type
per_column.rationale: Categorizes the clinical presentation (acute symptoms, chronic management, injury/trauma, etc.) derived from the visit reason. This is a distinct clinical dimension that plausibly steers routing to departments without restating department directly.

per_column.name: acute_vs_chronic
per_column.rationale: Onset/temporality of the condition. This carries signal about department (e.g., acute onset -> emergency/acute care) and is not a component or restatement of department.

per_column.name: primary_system
per_column.rationale: Organ/body-system involved (cardiac, musculoskeletal, dermatologic, etc.). This is the strongest legitimate predictor since specialty departments map closely to body systems, yet it is a separate clinical attribute, not the department label itself.

per_column.name: severity_level
per_column.rationale: Clinical severity (mild, moderate, urgent, life-threatening). Provides predictive signal for triage/department assignment and is independent of the department label. Overlaps somewhat with existing urgency but adds granularity.

per_column.name: population_context
per_column.rationale: Patient population/age band. Relevant to department (e.g., pediatric vs adult), though it largely duplicates the existing age_group column, reducing incremental value; still a legitimate non-leaking predictor.

judge.rationale: All five columns are legitimate, non-leaking predictors derived from the clinical presentation rather than restatements or deterministic functions of department. primary_system and presentation_type carry the most department-discriminating signal; acute_vs_chronic and severity_level add triage-relevant dimensions; population_context is valid but partly redundant with the existing age_group column. As a set they provide substantial genuine predictive leverage beyond the original columns, discounted modestly for overlap with existing urgency/age_group and the coarse severity/urgency correlation.
